The current app scored 8.06/10 in three baseline rounds. Both alternatives scored 10.00/10, but reviewers preferred different designs for different tasks. The clearest opportunity is the task editor. In the current app a date runs off the screen, and two property controls show only icons. All three baseline reviewers scored the editor 6/10. Both alternatives fit the complete dates and five named properties on screen.

What changed

Fieldnotes organizes work like a daybook. Serif task titles sit under Scheduled or Unscheduled headings, deadlines appear beside the relevant task, and a labeled New task button anchors capture. The sections explain why a task appears. They also consume more vertical space. Reviewers flagged repeated “Today” labels on Planner and duplicate Workspaces controls in Inbox.

Index organizes work like a compact table. A week strip shows the neighboring dates, timing has its own column, workspace tabs stay visible, and a grid gives each editable property a labeled control. Reviewers pointed out that single-letter weekdays repeat, the Inbox capture button has only a plus, and the two date fields sit diagonally apart.

Where each design helped

Both concepts gained 3.06 points over the current screenshots in the same panel. Those unchanged screenshots averaged 6.94 on the repeat, about 1.1 points below their first rating. All 36 concept ratings reached the maximum despite recorded concerns. The absolute gains depend on the panel and the rubric has little resolution at its upper end.

After the scoring tie, three fresh reviewers saw the two concepts side by side. Each received the six screen pairs in shuffled order, with each design on the left three times. They could choose either side or a tie for the stated task. These follow-up choices were collected after scoring and do not change the numeric results.

How to read the scores

Six fresh Codex reviewer sessions used GPT-6.2-astra at high reasoning effort. Three first scored six current screens. After the concepts were drawn, three different reviewers each received all 18 images, shuffled with anonymous IDs. The same current screenshots appeared again as a control. Each image received five integer marks from 0 to 2 for orientation, scanability, affordance, legibility and composition. Every screen and reviewer counted equally.

Baseline images came from the iPhone 18 Pro Max simulator on iOS 27.2, 1320 × 2868 pixels, at app revision 4fe70da. Five screens use the capture-and-relaunch fixture. The editor uses the row-editing fixture. Both alternatives are HTML mockups rendered in headless Chrome at 440 × 956 points and 3× scale, with the corresponding app status strip. Each panel saw the same 420-pixel-wide image treatment. The task records, visible dates and selected day match within each comparison.

This sample contains only one or two tasks per list. Differences near the top of the rubric can be sensitive to one reviewer changing a single mark. The scores describe static screenshots. Thumb reach, task completion, larger text, VoiceOver and implementation feasibility still need direct testing.
